data.name: Sample - Fortinet FortiAIGate - 1.7.1
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Fortinet FortiAIGate" connector. If you are planning to use the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Renew Expiring FortiAIGate Keys in Vault
workflows.description:
Renews FortiAIGate virtual keys before they expire and puts each new secret into the HashiCorp Vault secret that holds it. FortiAIGate lists the keys that expire within Within (Days), and the ones already expired. Vault is then searched under Secret Folder for secrets whose custom metadata tag faig_key_id names one of those keys; Vault cannot search, so this lists the folder and reads each secret's metadata, never a secret value. A key with exactly one tagged secret is renewed by the child playbook "Renew FortiAIGate Key in Vault". A key no secret is tagged with is left to expire (no app uses it), and a key tagged on more than one secret is not touched and reported as a conflict, for a person.
Inputs: secret_folder (default lab), within_days (default 2) and extend_days (default 7; must be more than within_days, or every run would renew the same keys again). Outputs: expiring, renewed, failed, unused and conflicts. Run it from a schedule, for example every 15 minutes. The default HashiCorp Vault KV configuration needs read and list on the folder's metadata, patch on its metadata, and patch on its data - not read.

workflows.name: Renew FortiAIGate Key in Vault
workflows.description:
Renews one FortiAIGate virtual key and stores its new secret in the HashiCorp Vault secret that holds it. The key keeps its id, name, limits, policies and model access; its expiry moves to Extend By (Days) from now when it would come sooner. Only the api_key field of the secret is changed (an HTTP PATCH - other fields are kept), and the secret's metadata is stamped with faig_rotated_at and faig_expires_at. The new secret is then tested against the data plane.
If the renew is refused (a revoked key, say), outcome is renew_failed and nothing changes. If the Vault write fails, the run says so and stores the secret nowhere: the old secret is already dead, so fix Vault and run this again - a rotate can be repeated. Called by "Renew Expiring FortiAIGate Keys in Vault"; inputs key_id, secret_path, extend_days. Outputs: key_id, key_name, secret_path, outcome (renewed, renew_failed or write_failed), method, expires_at, verified.

groups.name: Note: RenewKey
groups.description: Errors are caught so the child always ends on a result (a revoked key, say), and one bad key cannot stop the parent's loop.

groups.name: Note: WriteSecret
groups.description: Changes only api_key. Retried on network and server errors.

workflows.name: Onboard FortiAIGate Key to Vault
workflows.description:
API endpoint that creates a FortiAIGate virtual key for an app and stores it in a NEW HashiCorp Vault secret, tagged so the renewal playbooks can find it. POST a JSON body: secret_path (required), key_name (default: the secret path), workspace (name or id), providers (default openai), expires_in_days (default 7) and fields (an object of extra secret fields, for example base_url and model).
The secret path must be free: the run checks first and writes with check-and-set 0, so an existing secret is never overwritten. If the Vault write fails, the new key is revoked, so no working key is left outside Vault. The secret's metadata gets faig_key_id, faig_key_name, faig_expires_at and faig_created_at. Ends with key_name, secret_path, key_id, expires_at and outcome (created, path_in_use or write_failed). The default HashiCorp Vault KV configuration needs create on the data path and read and patch on the metadata path.

groups.name: Note: PathAllowed
groups.description:
Checked before any Vault call, so the caller gets a result, not a failed run.
The regex is an allowlist: alphanumerics, underscore, hyphen, dot and
forward slash only, starting on a non-dot. That alone kills backslash,
null byte, percent-encoded tricks, scheme prefixes and absolute paths;
the explicit `..`/`.` segment check kills a path that is otherwise all
allowed chars but still walks the tree.

workflows.name: Revoke FortiAIGate Key on Guardrail Block
workflows.description:
API endpoint that reacts to a FortiAIGate guardrail block (DLP, ATLAS or any detector verdict the gateway refuses): revokes the bad virtual key, clears the Vault secret that holds it, then rotates every other key stored under the same workspace so a run cannot leave a working peer behind. POST a JSON body: key_id (required), workspace_id, policy (name of the guardrail that blocked, kept in metadata for audit), request_id (the FortiAIGate request uuid, kept in metadata), secret_folder (default lab), extend_days (default 7, used when rotating peers), max_peers (default 25).
The bad key is revoked FIRST so the attacker cannot use it while the run is still working. The Vault secret keyed by its faig_key_id tag has its api_key replaced with "REVOKED" (apps that read it fail-closed) and is stamped with faig_revoked_at, faig_revoked_policy and faig_revoked_request. Peers are the other secrets tagged with the same faig_workspace_id - rotated through the child "Renew FortiAIGate Key in Vault". If no peers are tagged (the workspace has one app, or the backfill has not run), peers_rotated is empty and the run still ends green - the bad key is already dead. Over the max_peers cap, the run ends with outcome=too_many_peers and no peer is rotated.
Debug mode is on so the API caller can read the summary from the last step. That also stores step results (the new peers' secrets) in the run history until the next rotation or log purge.

groups.name: Note: ParseRequest
groups.description: The API body arrives as a raw JSON string in vars.request.body.

groups.name: Note: VerifyBlock
groups.description: Look the request_id up in the FortiAIGate traffic logs. The record names the virtual key that sent the request and the verdict the gateway returned - so a caller cannot name a key that was not actually blocked.

groups.name: Note: BlockVerified
groups.description: A match is only accepted if the block fired within the last 15 minutes (900000 ms). An older uuid is a replay - a privileged caller could otherwise reuse any past block to revoke an arbitrary key later.

groups.name: Note: TrustedWorkspace
groups.description: Pull faig_workspace_id and the prior faig_revoked_request from the bad secret's metadata (set by onboarding and the previous run). The workspace must come from Vault, not the caller's body; the prior request id lets us refuse a replay of the same fresh request.

groups.name: Note: AlreadyProcessed
groups.description: If this request_id is already stamped on the secret, a prior run already revoked the key and rotated its peers. Refuse the replay.

groups.name: Note: ClearSecret
groups.description: Patch api_key to REVOKED; other secret fields (base_url, model) are kept.

groups.name: Note: HaveWorkspace
groups.description: Empty workspace could over-match - skip peer rotation and end with revoked_no_peers.

groups.name: Note: RevokeFailed
groups.description: Revoke was refused by the gateway. Do NOT clear Vault - app is still live on the current secret.

groups.name: Note: RevokeOrphan
groups.description: No Vault secret is tagged with this key - it is either an unmanaged key or one not yet backfilled. We still revoke it.

groups.name: Note: FindPeers
groups.description: Peers are the OTHER secrets tagged with this workspace. The bad secret shares the tag, so we filter it out next.

groups.name: Note: PeerCount
groups.description: Drop the bad secret from the peer list.

groups.name: Note: StampCompleteNoPeers
groups.description: Same completion marker as the peer path, so a replay with no peers also dedupes.

groups.name: Note: RotatePeers
groups.description: One child run per peer. apply_async=false so the summary step sees the children's set_variable outputs.

groups.name: Note: StampComplete
groups.description: Dedup marker on the bad secret so a replay with the same request_id short-circuits.

groups.name: Note: VerificationFailed
groups.description: FortiAIGate traffic logs do not confirm a block for this key_id - do nothing.

groups.name: Note: AlreadyProcessedTerminal
groups.description: Replay of the same request_id - the first run already handled it.

groups.name: Note: AlreadyRevokedTerminal
groups.description: Key was already revoked - do not re-run peer rotation.

workflows.name: Heal Expired FortiAIGate Key in Vault
workflows.description:
Keeps an application's FortiAIGate virtual key working. Reads the key from a HashiCorp Vault KV v2 secret and tests it against the data plane. If it no longer works, the playbook renews the same key - an expired key is extended (FortiAIGate only rotates an active key) and then rotated - writes the new secret into the same Vault path as a new version, and checks that the new secret works. The key keeps its id, name, limits, policies and model access; every other field of the secret is kept. A key that still works is left alone, and a revoked or suspended key stops the run with a message.
Inputs: secret_path (the KV v2 path, for example lab/ai) and, when the key is not stored under api_key, key_field. Outputs: rotation_result (a one-line outcome), rotated (true or false), key_id and key_method (rotated or extended_and_rotated). Run it from a schedule, or call it as a child playbook once per secret.

arguments.rotation_outcome: failed - new secret rejected by the data plane

arguments.rotation_result: {{ vars.rotation_outcome | default("renewed - new secret stored in Vault and verified") }}

groups.name: Note: ResolvePath
groups.description: The Vault path of the secret holding the key, and the field it is stored in. Read from the playbook parameters (manual run, schedule, child call) or, for an API trigger that sends them as top-level variables, from vars.

groups.name: Note: KeyValid
groups.description: Branch on the data-plane verdict for the stored key.

groups.name: Note: RenewKey
groups.description: Same key, new secret. FortiAIGate only rotates an active key, so an expired one is extended first.

groups.name: Note: BuildPayload
groups.description: KV v2 writes create a new version and drop omitted fields, so the new secret data is the whole current secret with only the key field replaced. Built as a JSON string because connector params are strings.

groups.name: Note: NewKeyValid
groups.description: The new secret must validate; anything else fails the run.

groups.name: Note: FailRotation
groups.description: Reachable only when the new secret does not validate.

groups.name: Note: Done
groups.description: Terminal summary.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Wizard-editable defaults. `range` is the backfill window used while the
watermark is missing or '0'. The macro name is scoped to this playbook's UUID,
so two ingestion configurations never share a watermark.

groups.name: Note: Environment Setup
groups.description:
Runs when the watermark macro does not exist yet, not only on the wizard's
`vars.request.env_setup` first pass. It must come AFTER Get Macro Value so its
absence can be seen: Update Last Pull Time only updates the macro, it does not
create it, so a missing macro would otherwise leave the watermark unwritten and
every run would read the backfill window again without any error.
The macro is primed to '0', which Set Time Configuration reads as a cold start.

groups.name: Note: Set Time Configuration
groups.description:
`curr_timestamp` is the end of this run's window, 60 seconds behind the clock
(see the block comment above). It is written back to the macro only after Ingest
succeeds, so a failed run reads its window again. `last_pull_time` is empty on a
cold start (macro missing, or '0'): the run then reads `range` instead, and
`until` stays empty because a custom window needs a start.

groups.name: Note: Mapping Preview
groups.description:
The Data Ingestion Wizard runs the Ingest playbook with
`vars.request.env_setup == true` while the analyst designs the field mapping in
the UI. In that mode the first fetched record is returned so the wizard can
render the Data Mapping preview; no alerts are written. `false` (or missing)
is the real ingestion path.

groups.name: Note: Return Sample
groups.description:
The sample for the wizard's Data Mapping preview: the first blocked request of
the window, whose keys are the fields `Create Record` maps. Falls back to a
representative record when the window is empty, so the preview still renders.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
The values the alerts take from the connector's output: the window's records
and the macro that holds its watermark. The severity is fixed in Create Record.

groups.name: Note: Create Record
groups.description:
The step is named "Create Record" because the Data Ingestion Wizard's Data
Mapping page is shown only for a create playbook with a step of exactly that
name, and it reads the target module off this step.

`is_upsert` routes this at /api/3/upsert/alerts, keyed on sourceId (the blocked
request's uuid), so a window read twice updates its alerts. Without it the plain
insert path 409s on the sourceId uniqueness constraint.

Only the alert fields below are set. Everything the gateway recorded is kept as
JSON in sourcedata (sourcedata must stay `| toJSON`: a bare {{ }} on a dict is
stored as the literal string "Array").

groups.name: Note: Update Last Pull Time
groups.description:
Advances the watermark only after the alerts are written, so a failed Create
Record leaves the window to be read again.
